$comment: The source of sf-icon's element plumbing (core/js/element-manifest.js). Taken from simai/ui-control control/smart-architecture/migration/out/icon (migration/convert-1.3.8.mjs over simai/ui-source@5100227); standard simai.smart-component 1.3.8, vocabulary 1.1.5. Every x-todo of the conversion is decided: x-decisions says how.

badge-count.summary: A count on the icon (simai/ui-source#12): a whole number above 0 shows, 0 or empty hides the badge. Above badge-cap it reads «<cap>+»; the exact number joins the icon's accessible name («Почта, 3 непрочитанных») and the badge's tooltip. On an anchor of size 1/3 or 1/2 a count is drawn as a dot.

badge-dot.summary: A dot on the icon, a count with no number: something new. Shown when badge-count is not set; with a count, the count is drawn as a dot. Its text equivalent («есть новое» / «new» by default, badge-label to change it) joins the accessible name.

badge-cap.summary: The largest count drawn as a number; a larger one reads «<cap>+».

badge-label.summary: The words the badge adds to the accessible name and its tooltip, in place of the page language's default: for a dot the whole text equivalent; for a count the phrase in plural forms separated by «|» (one|few|many in Russian, one|other in English) with {count} where the number goes.

loaded.summary: The exact subset that draws this glyph is in place; synchronized from the Loader, never an authoring switch

default.$comment: The Lit template in JavaScript, the migration form of §5.2 (§16): the build does not compile template.html yet, so a second copy of the markup would only drift from the one that draws.

accessibility.$comment: img while label is set (the glyph, or the badge anchor, carries role=img and the label as its name); without label the glyph is decorative and aria-hidden, and the badge phrase is said in hidden words.

aliases.$comment: Dated aliases of sf-icon for the shim (stands/18-aliases-ci/alias.mjs, standard §16 item 20). mode: same-detail (the shim sends the new and the old name), split / detail-adds (a detail adapter, refused by the shim), attribute-and-property, method, property, manifest-only (the DOM name does not change), host-attribute (no shim), retired.

rows.note: the family's old name; the attribute is written with sharp

x-summary: Semantic Material Symbol wrapper with exact Loader tracking, accessible decorative or informative modes and token-owned geometry.
x-renamed: lang runtime also holds the words of ANCHORED_BADGE_TEXT (ui-source/src/component/badges/js/_anchored-state.js): a shared script this component draws with (§11: no word lives only inside a bundle)
x-decisions: a11y-role: img while label is set, none otherwise: an unlabelled glyph is decorative and aria-hidden (the control around it owns the name). One role, as accessibility.$comment says; the name comes from label alone.

loaded moves from settings to values: it is what the Loader reports (the exact subset is in place), not an authoring switch; it keeps its default, so a page that wrote loaded still writes the attribute (§4, §4.3).

type keeps its name: here it is the font family (outlined, rounded, sharp), not the appearance axis of contracts/public-api-axes.json. Its old value shape is a dated value alias of sharp (aliases.json), no longer a value of the enum.

number settings: weight (100–700, step 100), grade (-50–200), optical-size (20–48) and badge-cap declare the bounds the code clamps to (§4.2, §16 item 29). badge-count stays a string: it takes the text a page gives and is capped by badge-cap.
template: templates.default names the Lit template js/templates/default.js, the migration form §5.2 allows; no template.html until the build compiles one (a copy nothing draws would drift).
examples: examples.json from studio.fixture.json (home, size 1) plus a labelled icon, filled and rounded, a weight, a count badge and a dot badge.

css-variables: five public variables (ink, glyph size, the weight and fill axes, line height), read by the class sheet with the internal token as fallback (§6) and listed in src/core/contracts/public-variables.v1.json. The ink is the base layer's: a component that sets its icons' ink (--sf-icon--color) still wins inside it.
words: the badge phrase (count, dot) is lang runtime, read by the shared anchored-badge helper (x-renamed).

folder: icons takes the tag's name, icon (§3, §21, §16 item 16); the loader bundle is cl-icon, cl-icons is a Loader forward (src/core/contracts/smart-rule-forwards.v1.json) and smart/icons/js/icons.js a forwarding script until 2026-12-01 (change journal path-smart-icons-to-icon). The registry id follows the folder: smart.icon (smart.icons is its dated alias in the same record).
version 1.1.0: loaded moves to values and shape becomes a dated alias; no member is removed (§4.10).

version 1.1.1: the first-paint snapshots are retaken: the JSON island is printed once (no held copy), the icon font's state (sf-icon loaded, sf-icon-loaded) is left out, a closed surface prints closed and a size or place the code measured (a non-zero px width, height, inset, clip or transform) is left out, so a snapshot is the same on every run.

version 1.1.3: the bundle carries no element layer of its own -- element-manifest, aliases, the alias table, the host port, deprecations, page actions, the layer stack, the open-surface mark and the instance path come from the page's shared runtime (SF.runtimeModule, runtime ABI 1, core.runtime 1.1.0), one instance per page -- and embeds of this file only the keys the runtime reads. Behaviour unchanged.

$comment-after: The bundle's former name cl-icons (the folder was `icons` until standard
1.3.8 §3, §21 gave it the tag's name) is not a rule here: a rule of type
smart is a Smart component to the registry, and this one has no element. The
Loader forwards it to cl-icon from src/core/contracts/

ai_guidance.use_when: Use sf-icon for a Material Symbol that must participate in the Framework Loader and token scale. Omit label when adjacent text or a named control already conveys the meaning; provide a concise label only for an informative standalone symbol.
do_not: Do not copy generated ui-smart code
Do not move host data or access decisions into the component
Do not make the icon focusable or use it as a control
Do not label a decorative icon inside an already named control
Do not use loaded as an authoring switch

accessibility.focus: The icon is not interactive and never enters the tab order. Name the containing control instead.
